# High-dimensional projection heteroscedasticity test

<small>Source: [`R/modern_diagnostics.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/modern_diagnostics.R) · Help: `?performHighDimensionalTest`</small>

Applies principal component projections to the design matrix and evaluates a
Breusch-Pagan style statistic on the reduced representation. The procedure is
designed for settings where the number of predictors rivals or exceeds the
sample size.

## Usage

```r
performHighDimensionalTest(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  variance_threshold = 0.9,
  max_components = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object describing the mean structure whose
    residual variance is to be assessed.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default.
    The response, design, weights and offset are read from the fit itself, so
    a model that transforms its variables, has an `offset()` term, or takes
    its `weights` or `offset` from a column of the data needs no `data`, and
    the model frame of `model` is accepted as `data` (since 0.16.0; before,
    such models needed `data`). Data that are given are matched to the
    observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any
    order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data
    frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the
    order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit
    dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the
    observations of the fit are refused; see [test\_results](test_results.md).

`variance_threshold`
:   Proportion of predictor variance that the selected
    principal components should explain. Defaults to 0.9.

`max_components`
:   Optional upper bound on the number of principal
    components to retain. Defaults to `min(10, n - 5)`.

## Value

An `htest` object summarising the chi-squared statistic
of the auxiliary regression on principal component scores.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Fan, J., & Lv, J. (2008). Sure independence screening for ultrahigh dimensional
feature space. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 70*(5),
849–911.

## Examples

```r
set.seed(123)
X <- matrix(rnorm(80 * 20), nrow = 80)
beta <- c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, 15))
y <- X %*% beta + rnorm(80, sd = 0.5 + 0.2 * scale(X[, 1]))
df <- as.data.frame(cbind(y = as.numeric(y), X))
model <- lm(y ~ ., data = df)
performHighDimensionalTest(model, df)
```
